news.headline: uniQure Receives $65.00 Consensus Price Target from Brokerages
news.summary: Seventeen research firms covering uniQure now carry an average "Moderate Buy" rating (13 buy, 3 hold, 1 sell) and a consensus 12-month price target of $65.00. The bullish tilt follows July's Q2 update confirming the AMT-130 accelerated-approval pathway and the on-track Q3 2026 BLA/MAA filing timeline.

news.headline: uniQure Q2 2026 Earnings Call: Confirmatory Trial Design Detailed, Net Loss Widens
news.summary: Management said the FDA wants the AMT-130 post-approval confirmatory study to use a randomized standard-of-care control arm with Total Functional Capacity at 36 months as the primary endpoint, and that uniQure is already preparing the study. Net loss widened year-over-year on higher R&D spend even as the accelerated-approval regulatory path firmed up.

news.headline: Wells Fargo Raises uniQure Price Target to $75, Maintains Overweight
news.summary: Wells Fargo lifted its price target on uniQure to $75 from $60 while reiterating an Overweight rating, citing the cleared AMT-130 accelerated-approval path plus encouraging early AMT-260 epilepsy data (up to 100% seizure reduction in low-dose patients) as an added pipeline catalyst.

news.headline: Wolfe Research Upgrades uniQure to Outperform, Sees 70% Odds of AMT-130 Approval
news.summary: Wolfe Research upgraded uniQure to Outperform from Peer Perform with a $65 price target, arguing the market is underpricing AMT-130's approval odds (Wolfe models ~70% vs. the market's implied under-50%) and estimating peak U.S. sales of $2 billion if approved.

news.headline: uniQure Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Company Update
news.summary: uniQure reported Q2 revenue of $5.8M (ahead of consensus) and cash, cash equivalents and investments of $810.3M, extending its runway into 2030 after the June $259M offering. The company confirmed it remains on track to submit the AMT-130 BLA (US) and MAA (UK) in Q3 2026, with topline 4-year Huntington's data expected in September 2026.

news.headline: uniQure Update: AMT-191 Fabry Dosing Remains Paused Pending FDA Liver-Monitoring Agreement
news.summary: uniQure reported dose-dependent increases in alpha-Gal A enzyme activity across 11 Fabry disease patients dosed with AMT-191, but additional dosing in the mid- and high-dose cohorts remains paused pending FDA agreement on a monitoring plan following Grade 3 liver enzyme elevations in two patients.

catalysts.label: AMT-130 4-year topline data
catalysts.detail: Topline 4-year follow-up safety/efficacy data (24 patients: 12 low-dose, 12 high-dose) from the Phase I/II Huntington's disease study expected, updating the 3-year cUHDRS progression-slowing result. Not yet reported as of 2026-08-30.

catalysts.label: AMT-130 BLA submission to FDA
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans to submit the Biologics License Application for AMT-130 under the accelerated approval pathway, using 3-year Phase I/II data versus an Enroll-HD external control as the primary basis; reaffirmed on the Aug 7 Q2 earnings call and not yet submitted as of 2026-08-30.

catalysts.label: AMT-130 UK MHRA MAA submission
catalysts.detail: Marketing Authorisation Application planned for the UK following a positive MHRA pre-submission meeting, run in parallel with the US BLA.

catalysts.label: AMT-260 epilepsy second cohort enrollment complete
catalysts.detail: Enrollment in the second, higher-dose cohort of the Phase I/IIa refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy trial expected to complete.

catalysts.label: Possible FDA Advisory Committee (AdCom) meeting
catalysts.detail: Management expects and is preparing for a likely FDA AdCom review of the AMT-130 BLA given it would be the first Huntington's disease therapy, though no formal request has been made.

catalysts.label: AMT-260 / AMT-191 program updates
catalysts.detail: Updated clinical data expected for the refractory epilepsy (AMT-260, both dose cohorts) and Fabry disease (AMT-191) gene therapy programs.

pulse: uniQure enters the final stretch before its September 2026 catalyst window well capitalized ($810.3M cash as of Q2, runway into 2030 after the June $259M raise) and with a cleared regulatory path: the FDA has agreed 3-year Phase I/II data can support an accelerated-approval BLA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease, still on track for filing in Q3 2026 alongside a parallel UK MAA. Wall Street sentiment has turned more bullish into the readout, with Wolfe Research and Wells Fargo among firms raising targets ($65 and $75 respectively) and the broader analyst consensus near $65 (Moderate Buy); the stock trades in the low-$50s, up sharply from its March 2026 FDA-scare lows but still well below its October 2025 52-week high near $71.50. The next major catalyst is topline 4-year AMT-130 data expected imminently in September 2026, with management also flagging a likely FDA Advisory Committee review as a probable extra step before approval; earlier-stage programs are more mixed, with encouraging AMT-260 epilepsy seizure-reduction data offset by AMT-191 Fabry dosing that remains paused pending an FDA liver-safety monitoring agreement.
